department: Department of Nanoengineering (Joint School of Nanoscience and Nanoengineering)

deadline.value: Departmental priority deadline for fellowships and departmental assistantships is February 1 (Fall admission only; December 15 suggested for university fellowships; international deadline June 1; final deadline July 1).
deadline.quote: The first deadline is a departmental deadline of February 1st for applicants who wish to be considered for University fellowships and departmental assistantships; ... The second deadline is July 1st for all remaining applicants; after this deadline, the university’s application system closes. ... International applications must be received by June 1st.

gre_general.value: GRE is not required under holistic review, though JSNN strongly encourages applicants without an accredited U.S. degree to submit GRE scores to improve admission and funding chances (overview bullet and N.C. A&T summary page still list GRE scores).
gre_general.quote: No. The Department of Nanoengineering uses a holistic approach to evaluate all applicants to our program, and the GRE is not required to gain admission to our program. However, we strongly encourage students who have not earned a degree from an accredited US institution to submit GRE scores so as to increase their likelihood of admission and financial support.

gre_subject.value: ETS does not offer a GRE Subject Test in Materials Science or Nanoengineering.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: JSNN strongly recommends contacting a prospective faculty advisor before applying, and requires listing 1 to 3 potential advisors in the application.
supervisor.quote: It is strongly recommended you connect with a prospective faculty advisor via telephone or email prior to applying to the program. ... for a complete application, we require ... the selection of one to three potential advisors.

funding.value: Admitted Ph.D. students are guaranteed two years of departmental assistantship support, with an additional two years available upon reaching Ph.D. candidacy; nearly 94% of JSNN students receive assistantships and/or tuition waivers.
funding.quote: Students admitted into either program—at UNC Greensboro or North Carolina A&T State University—are guaranteed two years of departmental assistantship support, with an additional two years available upon achieving Ph.D. candidacy. | Currently, nearly 94% of students receive some form of graduate assistantship and/or tuition waiver.

entry_route.value: A bachelor's degree in any engineering, natural science, or physical science field (with Calculus I and II) is required for entry into the Nanoengineering Ph.D. program.
entry_route.quote: A Bachelor’s degree in any engineering, natural or physical sciences field is a requirement for entering the Ph.D. program in the Department of Nanoengineering.

notes: Offered at the Joint School of Nanoscience and Nanoengineering (JSNN) with a Special Concentration in Synthetic Biology. Applications are submitted through the N.C. A&T Graduate Admissions portal ($60 portal fee; JSNN's departmental FAQ cites $65). Fall entry only.
